reviews.evidence: README shows a shipped cross-host memory protocol with curation, bounded-index enforcement, validation, continuity sync, reader adapters, init helpers, and detailed lifecycle guidance.
reviews.concern: It provides almost no concrete visible memory input/output demonstration, and repeatedly notes best-effort enforcement plus single-writer, personal-scale limits.

reviews.evidence: README documents database connection, schema exploration, natural-language SQL analysis, governance, follow-up analysis, dashboards, and offline HTML reports, with Web/TUI paths and five concrete business scenarios.
reviews.concern: Reliability evidence is concentrated on supported databases, local execution, credential handling, and read-only protection; tests and troubleshooting coverage are not shown.

reviews.evidence: README presents a comprehensive terminal coding-agent system spanning interactive and headless runs, persisted sessions, skills, permissions, hooks, lazy MCP, sub-agents, tools, models, and detailed command/config references.
reviews.concern: Demonstrations emphasize interface and measured footprint/cache behavior rather than representative coding-task outcomes, and there is no comparably broad troubleshooting section.

reviews.evidence: README states a coherent catalog workflow: discover public topic-tagged repositories, inspect a small candidate set, distinguish installation forms, explain choices, run a security preflight, then install and verify after user selection.
reviews.concern: Only two brief discovery scenarios are given, with no concrete candidate comparison, security report, installation result, or verification output.

reviews.evidence: README describes shipped novel and short-drama workbenches with numerous skills and roles, structured production artifacts, native three-column editing, file following, previews, and two workflow GIFs.
reviews.concern: Operational guidance stops near choosing /story or /short-drama, so the creative workflows themselves lack detailed happy paths, choices, and representative finished artifacts in the README.

reviews.evidence: README documents an unusually comprehensive compatibility system, full lifecycle commands, advanced MCP walkthrough, numerous runnable scenario examples, explicit capability mappings, real end-to-end validation records, limitations, gaps, and recovery guidance.
reviews.concern: The broad top-50 probe table is explicitly weaker than real workflow validation, with two exercises pending rerun and four mapped surfaces unavailable.

reviews.evidence: README covers aggregated search, conversational paging, resource details, magnet/torrent handling, optional streaming, settings, migration, updates, acceptance steps, screenshots, and extensive troubleshooting and security boundaries.
reviews.concern: The explicit user scenarios are few and brief, and the streaming path deliberately excludes dynamic rules while relying on user-supplied site rules and third-party availability.

reviews.evidence: README shows a full GUI/TUI coding distribution with shared sessions, workspaces, configurable presets and models, Host supervision, broad CLI operations, source/release workflows, diagnostics, cache recovery, and platform/version boundaries.
reviews.concern: Visible demonstrations are limited to one GUI and one TUI screenshot, and the project remains a developer preview whose upstream compatibility and release availability may change.

reviews.evidence: README demonstrates a comprehensive office environment across Sheets, Docs, Slides, Bases, and Boards, with natural-language creation, import/export, isolated drafts, verification, review, detailed case workflows, screenshots, linting, limits, and timeout/fallback controls.
reviews.concern: Some slide checks require local Chrome, several advanced Slide and Board features remain unsupported, and Board file export is unavailable.

reviews.evidence: README shows a broad note application and agent integration with multiple themes, images, multi-note storage, synchronization, DSH and skill-driven export, AI polishing, Markdown/HTML/image outputs, WeChat transfer, Docker deployment, and many screenshots/GIFs.
reviews.concern: Operational detail is strongest for one DSH export prompt, one skill prompt, and deployment; tests, failure behavior, and troubleshooting are sparse relative to the breadth of claims.
